job_title: National Sales Manager - BUCO & TimberCity - Cape Town
about_role:
Introduction:
Lead, develop and execute the national sales strategy for the B&T Division to accelerate market-led growth, increase trade market share, improve customer visibility and deliver sustainable profitable revenue growth across all regions.
Description:
Strategic Sales Leadership
• Develop and implement a national sales strategy aligned to divisional and company growth objectives.
• Establish annual, quarterly and monthly sales plans and targets.
• Drive sustainable revenue growth, market share expansion and margin improvement.
• Develop trade-focused customer growth strategies to increase market penetration.
• Identify market opportunities, customer trends and competitor activity to inform business decisions.
• Lead the execution of customer-led growth initiatives across all regions.
• Establish go-to-market strategies for key customer segments and target markets.
Sales Transformation and Operating Model Development
• Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the current sales operating model.
• Evaluate the effectiveness, productivity and structure of internal and external sales functions.
• Review customer segmentation, territory allocation, workload distribution and customer coverage models.
• Benchmark sales structures and performance against industry best practice.
• Develop recommendations regarding:
• National and regional sales structures.
• Sales resource requirements.
• Reporting lines and span of control.
• Territory design and customer allocation.
• Sales role definitions and accountabilities.
• Customer segmentation models.
• Sales governance frameworks.
• Lead the implementation of approved organisational and sales transformation initiatives.
• Establish a scalable and sustainable sales operating model that supports future growth.
Leadership and Team Development
• Lead, coach and develop Regional Sales Managers to deliver consistent sales performance.
• Build a high-performance sales culture focused on accountability, customer service and commercial results.
• Drive employee engagement and capability development within the sales function.
• Ensure performance management processes are effectively implemented.
• Identify succession talent and develop future sales leaders.
• Support recruitment, onboarding and development of sales personnel.
Sales Operations and Performance Management
• Establish and manage the national sales budget and sales targets.
• Implement standardised sales processes, methodologies and operating standards.
• Develop sales scorecards, KPIs and performance management frameworks.
• Drive accuracy in sales forecasting and pipeline management.
• Monitor regional sales performance and implement corrective action where required.
• Ensure effective utilisation of CRM and sales management systems.
• Drive continuous improvement in sales productivity and effectiveness.
Customer and Market Development
• Develop and strengthen relationships with major trade customers and key accounts.
• Drive customer acquisition, retention and customer growth strategies.
• Increase customer visibility and engagement across all regions.
• Expand share of wallet within existing customer portfolios.
• Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships and market development.
• Provide customer and market insights to support business planning and decision-making.
• Ensure customer expectations and service commitments are consistently achieved.
Governance, Compliance and Commercial Excellence
• Establish sales governance standards and operating disciplines across the business.
• Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures and commercial frameworks.
• Balance sales growth objectives with profitability and risk management requirements.
• Collaborate with all internal stakeholders to optimise business performance.
• Drive adoption of data-driven decision-making and sales analytics.
• Ensure consistency in customer engagement and sales execution nationally.
Reporting and Performance Analysis
• Prepare and present monthly, quarterly and annual sales performance reports.
• Provide meaningful sales analysis and recommendations to executive leadership.
• Monitor key sales and customer metrics to identify trends and opportunities.
• Measure the effectiveness of sales initiatives and transformation programmes.
• Report on progress against strategic growth priorities and sales transformation objectives.
Requirements:
Minimum Qualifications
• Degree in Business Management, Commerce, Sales, Marketing or related field.
• Relevant postgraduate qualification advantageous.
Experience
• Minimum 8-10 years sales leadership experience within a multi-site commercial environment.
• Minimum 5 years' experience in a senior sales management role.
• Proven experience leading geographically dispersed sales teams.
• Demonstrated success in developing and implementing national sales strategies.
• Experience in sales transformation, organisational design or operating model implementation.
• Experience within building materials, hardware, wholesale, retail or construction-related industries would be advantageous.
• Proven track record of delivering sustainable revenue and market share growth.

job_title: Product Manager - Card Program & Digital Payments
about_role:
Role Information
Position: Product Manager – Card Program & Digital Payments
Key Competencies:
• Card Issuance and BIN Management
• Detailed understanding of Payment Systems Architecture & Integration
• Digital Banking Products and Mobile Wallets
• Banking, Payment Regulatory and Compliance
Your Leader: Head of Product
The Team: The Product team forms an integral part of the Weaver Fintech business, collaborating with several departments, and is responsible for leading development and optimisation of products that deliver value to our customers, merchants, and the business.
Location: Cape Town, South Africa
Role Overview
The absolute legend of a Product Manager we're seeking will be responsible for building and scaling our soon to be launched card program. Working in partnership with our sponsoring bank, you'll manage our BIN Program, oversee the issuance of virtual and physical cards, and create a world-class mobile digital banking platform.
As a Product Manager for our Card Program, you will define the product strategy for our card program, manage the roadmaps, optimise adoption, feature ROI and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver a seamless, secure, and rewarding payment experience. This role is central to driving financial inclusion, customer engagement, and commercial growth across Weaver Fintech's expanding product portfolio.
You should have deep expertise in payment systems, card issuing , mobile banking applications, regulatory compliance (FICA/POPIA), and cross-functional stakeholder management across multiple banking and technology providers.
Weaver Fintech
Join an agile team at South Africa's fastest-growing fintech, where you'll work with disruptive payment solutions, AI adoption, and cutting-edge technology across our 3.7 million customer base within PayJustNow and Finchoice. Be part of a purpose-driven organisation making a real difference—driving the next wave of financial inclusion and transforming how South Africans access payments, credit, and mobile services.
Key Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Planning
• Set card programme strategy and objectives aligned to company goals and market opportunities.
• Maintain a focused roadmap for card issuance, mobile payments, tokenisation, and digital wallet features, informed by market analysis and customer feedback.
• Analyse competitors in digital banking to identify differentiators and growth areas.
• Optimise card programme economics for profitable growth, covering profit routing, interchange, fee structures, and strategies for activation, adoption, and retention.
Card Program Management & Bank Partnership
• Oversee the entire card issuance programme, covering BIN allocation, card production, inventory, and distribution.
• Work closely with the sponsoring bank to ensure compliance with agreements, regulations, and operational SLAs.
• Coordinate with card networks or third-party vendors on tokenisation, security, and network compliance.
• Specify card controls, including spending limits, permitted transactions, geographic use, and fraud prevention measures.
Payment Systems & Integration
• Design and deploy payment workflows: virtual cards, tap-to-pay, QR payments, and P2P transfers.
• Integrate with payment providers, acquiring banks, processors, and gateways.
• Ensure payment security: PCI DSS, 3D Secure, and tokenisation.
• Define requirements for payment APIs, webhooks, and real-time processing.
Commercial Performance and Revenue Management
• Build business cases for card features, estimating revenue from interchange, mark-ups, subscriptions, and premium tiers.
• Set pricing for card services, ATM withdrawals, and premium offerings.
• Track KPIs like activation rates, transaction volumes, feature use, ARPU, AMPU, retention, and CLV.
• Evaluate payment trends, fraud, and declines to boost authorisation rates and enhance customer experience.
Mobile App Development & User Experience
• Define app requirements following platform-specific design guidelines and best practices
• Collaborate with design and engineering teams to create intuitive card management interfaces, instant notifications, and transaction history views
• Oversee the implementation of mobile wallet capabilities including Google Pay, and Samsung Pay integration
Delivery & Execution
• Translate product requirements into clear Business Requirement Specifications, User stories, and Technical Documentation for engineering teams
• Manage agile development processes including sprint planning, backlog prioritisation, and release coordination.
• Review and collaborate with the UI design team to optimise the card payment flows from a Customer Experience perspective.
Stakeholder Engagement & Compliance
• Align product initiatives with internal teams, including executives, legal, compliance, risk, marketing, support, and finance.
• Ensure compliance with South African financial regulations (FICA, POPIA, National Payment System Act, SARB).
• Maintain communication with external partners: sponsoring bank, payment networks, regulators, and tech vendors.
Performance & Optimisation
• Monitor card program performance through analytics and feedback.
• Conduct A/B tests to increase engagement.
• Benchmark top digital banks for improvements.
• Enhance products using customer input and fraud data.
Desired Qualifications & Competencies:
• Product Leadership in Payments: 5+ years in product management for payments, card issuing, digital wallets, or mobile banking.
• Card Programme & BIN Management: Practical experience building or managing card programmes with in-depth knowledge of BIN sponsorship, card network rules, and issuer-processor relationships.
• Payment Systems Expertise: Strong grasp of payment rails (EFT, RTC, card networks), processing flows, authorisation/settlement, and security standards (PCI DSS, tokenisation, EMV).
• Banking Partnership Management: Demonstrated ability to collaborate with sponsoring banks at an operational level.
• Vendor & System Integration: Experience integrating with multiple vendors including card processors, gateways, fraud systems, and core platforms.
• Regulatory Compliance & Risk: Knowledge of South African financial regulations (FICA, POPIA, NPS Act), card network compliance, fraud prevention, and risk-based authentication.
• Agile Delivery: Skilled in Agile/Scrum, managing multiple projects, sprint planning, backlog grooming, and iterative releases in fast-paced fintech environments.
• Customer-Focused Development: Experienced in user research, gathering feedback, and translating payment requirements into intuitive user experiences.
• Commercial Acumen: Understanding of payment economics, interchange fees, revenue models, pricing strategies, and P&L management.
• Leadership & Communication: Strong organisational, collaborative, and communication skills, able to lead teams and explain payment concepts clearly.
• Technical Literacy: Quick to learn new payment systems, card platforms, and fintech applications.
What We Offer
We build our workplace on reciprocity and trust. Every team member commits to delivering their best work while supporting colleagues and customers alike. Strong, authentic relationships drive our success—we value transparency, equity, and the unique perspectives each person brings to our team.
Your Benefits & Growth
• Flexible Work Environment – Hybrid working arrangements designed around your productivity and life balance
• Professional Development – Comprehensive support through coaching programs, skills training, and educational bursaries to accelerate your career
• Employee Wellness – Access to our CareConnect employee assistance program for holistic wellbeing support
• Modern Technology – Cutting-edge architectures and tools that maximise efficiency and minimise repetitive work
• Recognition & Celebration – We acknowledge your milestones and achievements throughout your journey with us
• Team Connection – Regular team socials and company-wide events that strengthen our

When you spend years in finance, there comes a point where you want more than just managing a small, isolated corner of a ledger.
You want genuine ownership, executive visibility, and the space to act as a true 2IC.
We are recruiting a Johannesburg-based Finance Manager to serve as second-in-command to the Chief Financial Officer for a high-growth, project-based international consultancy operating across multiple global jurisdictions.
The Role: The ground-level transaction processing is already taken care of by dedicated team members.
Your role is to take full ownership of the accounting cycle, elevating the finance function from simply keeping the books to actively driving business decisions.
What You Will Own:
• Overseeing month-end closures, bank reconciliations, and intercompany accounts across four international legal entities.
• Preparing monthly management reporting packs, profit and loss statements, cash flow forecasts, and project margin tracking.
• Managing technical accounting areas including revenue recognition, statutory obligations, and transfer pricing documentation.
• Standing in for the CFO with delegated authority on banking, payment releases, and executive reporting. What You Need:
• Qualified CA(SA), ACCA, CIMA, SAIPA, or BCom with completed articles.
• 3+ years post-qualification experience with full month-end ownership in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment.
• Practical proficiency in Sage, QuickBooks, and advanced Excel.
• Strong South African VAT and SARS experience, with cross-border tax exposure preferred.
• Experience in project-based industries (fit-out, construction, engineering, or similar) is a strong advantage. If you are looking for a high-impact deputy role with direct access to executive leadership and a clear growth path, please email your CV directly to my inbox or send a direct message for details.

IMPORT & EXPORT CONTROLLER
Location: Mount Edgecombe, Durban
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: Market Related / Negotiable based on experience
Our client is looking for an experienced Import & Export Controller to join their team in Mount Edgecombe, Durban.
The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating and controlling the movement of international cargo, managing import and export shipments from booking through to final delivery, and ensuring that all documentation, customs and operational requirements are handled accurately and efficiently.
This is a hands-on position suited to someone with solid clearing and forwarding / freight forwarding experience, particularly strong practical import experience.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Manage import and export shipments from booking through to final delivery.
- Coordinate containerised, break-bulk and project cargo.
- Prepare and check shipping and import/export documentation.
- Prepare Bills of Lading, manifests, commercial invoices, packing lists and customs-related documentation.
- Coordinate with shipping lines, freight forwarders, clearing agents and transport companies.
- Liaise with international clients and provide regular shipment updates.
- Track containers and monitor shipment progress.
- Coordinate and monitor clearing and forwarding activities.
- Ensure customs and port requirements are met.
- Work with clearing agents regarding customs entries and shipment releases.
- Monitor warehouse entries, removals in bond and export entries.
- Identify and resolve documentation discrepancies, delays and operational issues.
- Monitor demurrage, detention and other shipping-related costs and escalate where necessary.
- Maintain accurate shipment records and ensure documentation is properly filed and available for audit purposes.
- Provide regular shipment status updates to management and clients.
- Ensure shipments progress within required deadlines and agreed service levels.
REQUIREMENTS
- Minimum 3--5 years' hands-on experience in Import & Export / Shipping / Freight Forwarding.
- Strong practical import experience is essential.
- Experience with both imports and exports.
- Solid understanding of clearing and forwarding procedures.
- Practical knowledge of:
- Warehouse entries
- Removal in Bond
- Export entries
- Customs and port procedures
- Shipping documentation
- Experience dealing with shipping lines, clearing agents, freight forwarders and transporters.
- Experience handling containers, break-bulk and/or project cargo.
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong communication and client liaison skills.
- Ability to manage multiple shipments simultaneously and work under pressure.
- Good computer literacy and Microsoft Office skills.
- Experience with ACS or a similar freight/logistics system will be advantageous.
IDEAL CANDIDATE
The ideal candidate will be an experienced and technically competent Import & Export Controller who understands the full international shipment process and can manage shipments proactively rather than simply perform administrative tasks.
You must be confident dealing with shipping lines, clearing agents, freight forwarders, transporters and international clients, and have the ability to identify potential problems and resolve or escalate them before they impact delivery.
You should be organised, reliable, detail-oriented and able to work in a fast-paced environment where deadlines are critical.

Faircape Health Institute, a division of the Faircape Group, provides comprehensive healthcare services across the Western Cape, with established expertise in sub-acute care, rehabilitation, long-term care, and healthy ageing.
Building on this clinical foundation, we are developing a Longevity and Preventative Health Centre that brings together medicine, advanced diagnostics, exercise science, technology, and personalised health interventions within a multidisciplinary clinical environment.
We are seeking an experienced and forward-thinking Biokineticist to become an integral part of this developing service. We are looking for a dynamic, engaging and evidence-driven practitioner who enjoys working with people, takes initiative, and is confident in a highly visible, patient-facing role. The ideal candidate will be curious about the intersection of exercise science, medicine, technology, and longevity, and will be adaptable, resourceful, and comfortable contributing ideas while helping to build and shape a new service.
This is not a conventional Biokinetics practice. Working alongside our Clinical Lead – Longevity & Preventative Medicine and broader multidisciplinary team, the successful candidate will use advanced strength and functional assessment tools, objective performance data, VALD technology, AI-integrated training equipment, and other technologies to assess physical capacity and develop highly personalised interventions.
Central to the role is a closed-loop approach: assess, identify, prescribe, set measurable targets, reassess, and adapt. The Biokineticist will take ownership of this process while also contributing to the development of the protocols, guidelines, and programmes that support the service.
Key Responsibilities

• Identify opportunities to incorporate emerging exercise technologies, assessment tools, and new approaches into the programme

• Exposure to VALD or comparable assessment technology, data-driven exercise platforms, or technology-enabled training equipment will be advantageous

The National Operations Specialist supports the National Operations Manager in overseeing the execution of operational, capital expenditure and maintenance initiatives across the property portfolio.
The role is responsible for ensuring that approved plans, budgets, operational standards and compliance requirements are consistently implemented at site level. The Specialist works alongside site-based Operations Managers, providing technical and execution support without replacing their day-to-day operational accountability.
The role also provides technical oversight of CAPEX project milestones, monitors operational and compliance performance, consolidates portfolio-level reporting and develops the technical, financial and operational exposure required for future portfolio-level leadership.
Key Responsibilities
CAPEX & Project Execution Oversight
• Monitor approved CAPEX and major maintenance projects against budget, scope, programme and quality requirements.

• Consolidate CAPEX spend tracking across the portfolio.
• Maintain an accurate national CAPEX execution schedule.
• Provide execution-level input into asset lifecycle planning through site condition assessments and completed project data.
• Coordinate with Operations Managers, contractors and appointed professionals on project execution.

• Identify inconsistencies, inefficiencies and gaps in operational execution and recommend corrective action.
• Project manage ad-hoc portfolio-level execution initiatives as directed by the National Operations Manager. Reporting & Portfolio Insights
• Consolidate precinct-level information into standardised national reporting.
• Report on CAPEX progress, compliance, building performance and equipment performance.
• Monitor operational systems and dashboards, including relevant building management and CAPEX tracking platforms, to ensure data integrity.
• Provide accurate and timely execution-level reporting and insights.
• Identify early warning indicators, risks and variances and escalate these to the National Operations Manager. Risk, Compliance & Governance
• Conduct regular site inspections to assess internal compliance and operational performance.
• Execute the portfolio's risk and compliance monitoring programme at site level.
• Track remediation of audit findings relating to the OHS Act, SANS requirements, National Building Regulations and insurance risks.
• Monitor progress towards the resolution of compliance issues.
• Verify site-level compliance with approved policies, procedures and operational standards.

Hub operating strategy and leadership

Provides challenge and decision support to the leadership team beyond administration.

Accountable for cost-to-serve, continuous cost optimisation, efficiency and productivity.
Owns business-case discipline for hub investments and resourcing decisions.

Engages Audit, People Risk and relevant regulators on hub operating and people-data governance matters.
Ensures decisions, records and controls are sound and defensible.
Performance, insight and decision support

Tracks progress, closes actions and escalates material issues to the Executive Head and enterprise leadership.
Provides decision-ready analysis on the hub’s most material choices
Team leadership and operating capability
Leads the hub operations team, including the Specialist and Team Coordinator, sets standards and builds operating capability.
Drives continuous improvement and change in how the hub works.
Represents the hub operationally to Shared Services, CoE and business HR Executive Heads.
Internal communications and team experience
Runs hub internal communications, including team updates, leadership messages and wider HR or business communications as needed.
Plans and delivers team events, offsites and engagement moments with the Team Coordinator.
Supports team experience through onboarding logistics, tools, access, workspace and day-to-day operational needs.

Ensures packs are accurate, consistent, current and on time.

FET English Home Language Teacher
Grades 8 – 12 | Radley Private School | Randburg, Johannesburg
Full-time | On-site | SACE Registered
Job purpose
Radley Private School is looking for a caring, experienced and enthusiastic FET-qualified English Home Language educator who is passionate about developing confident communicators, critical thinkers and independent young adults.
At Radley, education extends beyond academic achievement. We combine strong academics with entrepreneurial thinking, creativity, problem-solving and real-world learning. Our smaller classes enable educators to understand their learners as individuals and provide the focused support and challenge each learner needs to progress.
The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and delivering engaging English Home Language lessons across the FET Phase, with a strong focus on Grades 10–12, IEB assessment requirements and examination preparation. The educator will develop learners’ competence and confidence across literature, language, comprehension, writing, oral communication and critical analysis.
The role includes lesson preparation, assessment, evaluation and reporting on learner academic progress, intervention where learning gaps are identified, and comprehensive academic record keeping in accordance with school, IEB, Department of Education and legislative requirements.
We are looking for an educator who wants to make a meaningful impact in a deliberately small, progressive and entrepreneurial school environment.
Key responsibilities
• Teach English Home Language in the FET Phase, including Grades 8–12, and foster purposeful and measurable progression in learning.
• Plan and deliver engaging, academically rigorous lessons aligned with the CAPS curriculum and applicable IEB requirements.
• Prepare learners effectively for internal assessments, examinations and the Grade 12 IEB National Senior Certificate examination.
• Develop learners’ competence in:
• English language and grammar;
• comprehension and critical reading;
• prescribed literature, including novels, drama and poetry;
• literary analysis and contextual questions;
• creative writing;
• transactional writing;
• visual literacy;
• oral communication, prepared and impromptu speaking; and
• critical thinking and interpretation.
• Employ appropriate teaching and intervention strategies to improve learner performance and achieve agreed academic outcomes each term.
• Adapt teaching approaches to accommodate different learning needs, abilities and levels of academic performance.
• Prepare lessons taking into account curriculum requirements, subject developments, new teaching methodologies, assessment practices, technology and relevant real-world contexts.
• Encourage learners to develop an appreciation for language, literature and communication and to confidently express and defend their ideas.
• Develop learners’ ability to communicate effectively in academic, professional, entrepreneurial and everyday contexts.
• Plan, coordinate, administer, assess, evaluate and report on learner academic progress.
• Analyse assessment results and use performance data to identify learning gaps and implement appropriate academic interventions.
• Provide additional academic support and extra lessons where learning needs are identified.
• Set high-quality tests, examinations, assignments, projects and other assessment activities in accordance with curriculum and IEB requirements.
• Prepare accurate marking guidelines and memoranda and ensure that assessments meet the appropriate cognitive and academic standards.
• Maintain and administer the prescribed School-Based Assessment (SBA) programme and ensure that all assessment evidence is complete, accurate and appropriately stored.
• Moderate test and examination papers, assessment tasks and memoranda internally and, where required, externally.
• Ensure accurate and up-to-date learner attendance, assessment results, academic records and supporting documentation are captured within prescribed deadlines.
• Maintain comprehensive records, update databases and complete statistical or academic analysis as required by the school, Department of Education, IEB and other applicable authorities.
• Provide constructive, meaningful and timely feedback to learners to support their academic development.
• Communicate effectively and professionally with parents or guardians regarding learner progress, concerns and required interventions.
• Assist the Principal and school leadership with learner counselling, guidance, career development, discipline and the general welfare of learners.
• Support learners in developing independence, resilience, confidence, accountability and critical-thinking skills.
• Incorporate appropriate technology and digital resources into teaching, research, assessment and learner engagement.
• Use real-world and entrepreneurial contexts, where appropriate, to make English learning relevant, meaningful and engaging.
• Collaborate with fellow educators to promote academic excellence, consistency in assessment and continuous improvement in teaching practice.
• Participate actively in staff meetings, academic meetings, professional development, training and coaching initiatives.
• Contribute positively to Radley’s entrepreneurial and future-focused school culture.
• Perform or assist with appropriate non-teaching and administrative responsibilities, including school events, supervision, fire drills, first aid activities and other school operational requirements.
Skills, competencies & minimum criteria
• Must be suitably FET qualified to teach English Home Language.
• An appropriate and recognised four-year teaching degree or diploma from an accredited tertiary institution.
• The qualification must include English as an appropriate teaching methodology/specialisation for the FET Phase.
• Current SACE registration is essential and non-negotiable.
• A minimum of three years’ relevant teaching experience.
• Previous experience teaching FET English Home Language, particularly Grades 10–12, is strongly preferred.

job_title: Environmental, Sustainability and Governance (ESG) Data Analyst
about_role:
Sea Harvest is a proudly South African integrated fishing and food processing company, delivering quality seafood and food products to local and international markets. We are committed to sustainability, innovation and the development of our people.
An exciting opportunity exists for a suitably qualified and experienced ESG Data Analyst to join our team.
ROLE OVERVIEW:
To provide the data infrastructure, analysis and reporting systems that underpin both the Group's external ESG disclosure and its internal sustainability decision-making. Working closely with the Group Sustainability Manager, Finance and the operating businesses, the role ensures that ESG performance can be measured reliably, reported with confidence to the Group Exco and external stakeholders, and withstand external assurance.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Data platform and integrity
• Manage and maintain the Group's integrated ESG and GHG data platform, including collection, cleaning and validation of data from source.
• Establish and apply data-quality controls – consistent metric definitions, calculation methodologies, version control and a clear audit trail – to ensure data is verified, repeatable and assurance-ready.
• Ensure the business supplies data on time and that it is sanitised, checked and reconciled before use.
Inventory and metrics compilation
• Compile environmental performance data from wild capture vessels and aquaculture operations for the GHG inventory and IFRS S2 climate metrics, including marine fuel combustion (Scope 1, 2 and 3), refrigerant/fugitive emissions and purchased energy.
• Maintain emission factors and calculation tools in line with the GHG Protocol and calculate absolute and intensity metrics across the relevant entities (e.g. SHC, WPP).
Reporting and disclosure support
• Produce regular management dashboards for the Group Exco covering ESG KPIs, with trend and variance analysis.
• Support preparation of IFRS S1/S2 data, SASB disclosures and regulatory submissions with clean, verified data, and provide working papers and evidence to support external assurance.
• Track performance against agreed targets and flag data anomalies or emerging risks to the Group Sustainability Manager.
Engagement
• Liaise with operational data providers – vessel managers, factory and aquaculture sites – to secure complete and accurate source data.
QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS:
• A degree in environmental science, data/information science, statistics, finance/accounting, sustainability or a related field.
• Around 3 - 6 years' experience in a data, sustainability, reporting or analytical role.
• Advanced proficiency in Excel; exposure to ESG/carbon software or BI/dashboard tools (e.g. Power BI) is an advantage.
• Advantageous: training in GHG accounting / the GHG Protocol, or familiarity with ESG disclosure frameworks.
KEY COMPETENCIES:
• Strong data-management and analytical skills – data cleaning, validation, reconciliation and turning raw data into clear management information.
• Understanding of GHG accounting and ESG/climate metrics, ideally in an industrial or primary-industry context.
• Able to work across functions – comfortable chasing data from operations and collaborating with Finance.

job_title: Product Manager - MVNO, KYC, Rewards and Referrals
about_role:
Role Information
Position: Product Manager – MVNO, KYC, Rewards and Referrals
Key Competencies:
• KYC Regulatory Compliance & Identity Verification
• MVNO Operations / Telecommunications Product Management
• API Platform Development & Technical Product Leadership
• Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management in Regulated Industries Your Leader: Head of Product
The Team: The Product team forms an integral part of the Weaver Fintech business, collaborating with several departments, and is responsible for leading development and optimisation of products that deliver value to customers, merchants, and the business.
Location: Cape Town, South Africa
Role Overview
The absolute legend of a Product Manager we're seeking will be responsible for working within the Product development team to deliver new initiatives, enhancements, and resolve issues with a full understanding of the product development life cycle and have a track record of delivering changes, enhancements, and new functionality.
As a Product Manager, you will define product strategies, manage roadmaps, feature ROI and coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure successful delivery and continuous improvement. This role is central to driving innovation, customer satisfaction, and commercial impact across  Weaver Fintech’s product portfolio.
You should have strong expertise in regulatory compliance (KYC/AML), telecommunications operations (MVNO), product management methodologies, and cross-functional stakeholder management.
Weaver Fintech
Join an agile team at South Africa's fastest-growing fintech, where you'll work with disruptive payment solutions, AI adoption, and cutting-edge technology across our 3.7 million customer base within PayJustNow and Finchoice. Be part of a purpose-driven organisation making a real difference—driving the next wave of financial inclusion and transforming how South Africans access payments, credit, and mobile services.
Key Responsibilities
Product Strategy & Planning
• Define product vision, strategy, and goals in alignment with company objectives.
• Develop and maintain product roadmaps based on market insights, customer feedback, and business priorities.
• Conduct competitor analysis and identify opportunities for differentiation and growth.
Commercial Performance and Revenue Management
• Develop business cases, revenue projections, and ROI calculations; track product feature payback periods and P&L performance to ensure financial targets are met.
• Design and implement pricing models for features, bundles, and services that maximise revenue and margin; conduct pricing experiments and elasticity analysis to optimise feature pricing and packaging strategies.
• Monitor feature adoption rates, ARPU impact, and customer lifetime value (CLV); analyse key commercial KPIs including adoption rates, conversion rates, and revenue attribution to drive growth opportunities.
Delivery & Execution
• Translate product requirements into clear specifications and user stories.
• Collaborate with engineering, design, and QA teams to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
• Manage product launches and coordinate go-to-market activities with relevant stakeholders.
Stakeholder Engagement
• Work closely with internal teams (e.g. c-suite, marketing, sales, operations, finance) to align product initiatives.
• Act as the voice of the customer, ensuring product decisions reflect user needs and expectations.
Performance & Optimisation
• Monitor product performance using data and analytics to inform improvements.
• Conduct A/B testing and experimentation to validate hypotheses and optimise features.
• Gather feedback and iterate on products to enhance usability, engagement, and value.
Desired Qualifications & Competencies:
• Proven Product Leadership in Regulated Environments: 5+ years of product management experience in fintech, telecommunications, or other heavily regulated industries with demonstrated ability to ship compliant products at scale
• KYC/AML Domain Knowledge: Hands-on experience building or managing identity verification, customer onboarding, or compliance platforms with knowledge of regulatory frameworks (RICA / FICA)
• MVNO or Telecommunications Industry Experience: Direct experience with MVNO operations, mobile service provisioning, SIM lifecycle management, or telecom regulatory compliance
• Technical Proficiency & API-First Mindset: Strong understanding of API design, integration patterns, and platform architecture with ability to work closely with engineering teams on technical trade-offs and system design decisions
• Data-Driven Decision Making: Track record of using analytics, A/B testing, and quantitative metrics to drive product decisions, optimize conversion funnels, and measure success across compliance and business KPIs
• Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management: Demonstrated ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders including C-suite executives, legal/compliance teams, engineering, operations, and external partners (MNOs, regulators, vendors)
• Customer-Centric Product Development: Experience conducting user research, gathering customer feedback, and translating compliance requirements into seamless user experiences that balance regulatory needs with friction reduction

Role Summary:
The Service Charge Reconciliation Analyst is responsible for reviewing, validating, and processing service charge reconciliation invoices from landlords to ensure compliance with lease agreements, legal requirements, and internal policies. The role involves detailed financial checks, data analysis, communication with stakeholders, and accurate reporting to ensure the integrity and accuracy of real estate cost recoveries.

• Review and verify monthly invoices and annual operating expense reconciliations against lease terms, budgets, prior year bills, and legal documents.

• Validate mathematical accuracy of service charge invoices and supporting backup documentation; request clarification or correction from landlords as needed.
• Initiate and manage objection letters for disputed charges and track resolution in Salesforce.
• Use Sequentra and Salesforce systems to document and track invoice processing, validations, and communications.
• Follow the four-eye principle: complete initial checks and forward reconciliations for second-level validation and approval.
• Update financial systems with final approved charges and initiate conditional payments when required.
• Assist in the preparation of monthly and quarterly reports detailing reconciliation statuses, cost savings, and compliance metrics.
• Collaborate closely with landlords, CBRE internal teams, and client stakeholders to resolve disputes and ensure timely processing.

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field.
• Minimum 2 years of experience in accounts payable, lease administration, or real estate finance.
• Strong understanding of lease terms, operating expenses, and service charge structures.
• Excellent analytical skills and attention to detail, particularly with financial data.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills for professional correspondence and reporting.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with Salesforce, or similar systems is a plus.
• Ability to manage multiple reconciliations and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• Monitor vehicle utilisation and delivery performance.
• Ensure deliveries are completed within agreed timeframes.

• Analyze KPIs and identify trends.

Ligpos Employment Agency invites suitable candidates to apply for an exciting position at one of our premier clients in the hospitality industry.
Position Overview
• Location: Pretoria East
• Salary: R15,000 – R18,000 per month (Negotiable based on experience)
• Type: Full-Time (Includes weekends and night shifts on function days)
About the Role
Our client is looking for a strong, hands-on, and experienced Bar & Functions Supervisor to take full ownership of their Main Bar and general bar operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for stock control, stock counts, GAAP systems, cash-ups, reporting, and bar staff management.
Additionally, this role includes function supervision—particularly during the evening and closing periods. Once the main function coordinator wraps up their duties, you will take charge of the remaining function operations, staff breakdown, and venue lock-up.
Key Responsibilities
• Main Bar & Operations Management:
• Take full responsibility for the Main Bar and daily bar operations.
• Supervise, allocate, and prepare bar staff for service.
• Manage bar setup, operation, and breakdown.
• Stock & GAAP Control:
• Oversee bar stock, regular stock takes, and receiving incoming stock.
• Capture GRVs accurately and maintain GAAP records (essential).
• Manage stock allocation across bars while controlling wastage, breakages, and shortages.
• Cash-Ups & Reporting:
• Verify individual barmen cash-ups and perform final reconciliations.
• Identify discrepancies and submit all required bar reports promptly.
• Function Supervision & Venue Closing:
• Support the Function Coordinator during events.
• Take full charge of remaining operations once the main function team leaves.
• Oversee final staff duties, cleaning, stock returns, and secure the venue for the next event.
Requirements & Qualifications
• Experience: Proven experience in bar supervision or management.
• Systems: Strong background in stock control and GAAP experience is essential.
• Skills: Excellent leadership, numerical skills, and people management abilities.
• Personality: Confident, authoritative, reliable, and able to work independently under pressure.
• Availability: Comfortable working weekends and occasional late-night functions.
• Demographic Profile: Male candidate, preferably between 30 and 45 years of age.
Working Hours
• Monday – Friday: 09:00 – 16:00
• Saturday: 09:00 – 13:00

Role Purpose
This is a senior, head-of-function role operating at the commercial intersection of the business when a client goes live. The role is responsible for driving employee adoption, engagement and habitual use of Paymenow and its value-added services across client employee bases.
The role will develop and execute strategies that move employees from initial onboarding and awareness to sustained usage, working closely with clients and internal stakeholders to ensure successful activation and ongoing engagement.
This is not a traditional marketing or client service role. It requires a commercially minded individual who understands employee behaviour, change management, engagement and activation within large, often deskless, workforces.
Key Responsibilities
Employee Activation & Adoption
• Develop and implement employee activation strategies following client go-live.
• Drive awareness, adoption and habitual usage of Paymenow and its value-added services.
• Develop targeted engagement initiatives to increase employee participation and ongoing utilisation.
• Identify barriers to adoption and implement strategies to address them.
• Monitor employee engagement and usage trends and use insights to improve activation strategies.
• Develop approaches that encourage employees to move from initial awareness to sustained product usage. Client Go-Live & Onboarding
• Lead the employee-facing activation component of new client implementations.
• Work closely with internal teams and client stakeholders to ensure employees are effectively introduced to Paymenow.
• Develop onboarding and activation plans aligned to each client's workforce and operating environment.
• Coordinate communication and engagement activities throughout the implementation and post-launch lifecycle.
• Ensure activation plans are practical and effective for large and geographically dispersed employee populations. Change Management & Internal Engagement
• Develop and implement change management approaches that support product adoption.
• Translate product benefits into simple, relevant employee messaging.
• Design engagement initiatives suited to different workforce demographics and environments.
• Work with employer stakeholders to facilitate employee participation and adoption.
• Identify opportunities to improve the employee experience and strengthen product engagement. Field Activation & Workforce Engagement
• Develop activation strategies for large deskless workforces across sectors such as retail, logistics and manufacturing.
• Support or coordinate field-based activation initiatives where required.
• Develop practical engagement approaches for employees who may have limited access to traditional workplace communication channels.
• Leverage digital and mobile communication channels, including WhatsApp, to drive engagement at scale. Data, Reporting & Optimisation
• Monitor activation, engagement and usage metrics across client employee populations.
• Use data and feedback to identify trends, gaps and opportunities.
• Develop reports and insights for senior management and relevant stakeholders.
• Continuously test and optimise activation strategies based on employee behaviour and performance.
• Maintain accurate project and engagement information using CRM and project management systems. Function Development
•  Build and establish effective employee activation processes and frameworks.
• Develop scalable approaches that can be replicated across multiple clients and workforce environments.
• Identify opportunities to improve processes, systems and ways of working.
• Establish best practices for employee onboarding, activation, engagement and adoption.
• Contribute to the strategic development of the function as the business scales.

• Monitor and control access to the premises by documenting and regulating entrance into the site by vehicles or pedestrian’s access points to allow entry only to individuals with the correct authorization.
• Investigate and report signs of damage or unlawful entry as it occurs to management and act accordingly in the best interest of protecting Dis-Chem assets.
• Be professionally courteous and friendly, approachable, and willing to help others when receiving guests, customers, and employees.
• Protect the property and assets of the business from all dishonest persons, action or any acts of malicious behaviour that could result in the company suffering loss.
• Be always present at your post when on duty.
• Practice good customer service relations for all Dis-Chem internal and external customers.
• Report any unusual or suspicious behaviour by staff, customer, or suppliers.
• Opening and closing procedures-to be present observant and vigilant at the opening and closing of the site.
• Monitor surveillance CCTV footage in and around the distribution centre according to Dis-Chem standards.
• Monitor the alarm systems and or video cameras and operate detecting/ emergency equipment when needed.
• When working during the night or alone e.g., after hours render on-going surveillance of the premises by patrolling the grounds and using closed-circuit camera monitoring or alarm systems to detect and investigate suspicious activities to ensure that only legal entrance to the premises is maintained.
• In emergency situations provide assistance to the emergency teams e.g., alert first responders, clinic sisters, managers etc.
• Maintain order during evacuation procedures and at assembly points by providing exact directions or decisive actions to ensure the safety of lives and property by preventing stampedes and breakdown of law and order or illegal entrance to the premises.
• Offer on-going security advice and safety warnings and tips to ensure that all security and safety precautions are adhered to.
• Be vigilant - watch out for any suspicious activities that may mean a breach in security measures that have been put in place on the site.
• Interpret quickly whatever is seen and act accordingly.
• Respond quickly and correctly during crisis - be alerted to avoid being caught unaware.
• Know how best to respond to various dangerous situations according to industry and Dis-Chem standard operating procedures.
• During some very dangerous situations (such as armed robbery attacks or assaults with deadly weapons), waste no time in calling the police to prevent loss of lives or property.
• Take accurate notes of unusual occurrences and daily activities.
• Enforce rules and regulations to prevent criminal activity before it happens.
• Perform special duties - receive phone calls, respond to text, and email messages, and run vital errands for the department according to Dis-Chem and industry standard operating procedures.
• Maintain and complete all registers and occurrence books.
• Conduct legal and ethical investigations in line with Dis-Chem s standard operating procedures.
• Implement and ensure adherence to loss prevention policies, procedures, and best practices.
• Implement strategies to minimise financial losses caused by factors such as theft, accidents, injury and/ or vandalism
• Conduct audits as per business requirements and act accordingly.
• Adhere to Dis-Chem Policies and Standard Operating Procedures.
• Adhere to Health and Safety rules and regulations.

• PSIRA knowledge.

• Communication skills

• Recognises the need for procedures and follows relevant procedures.

• Finds solutions to potential issues as well as knowing when to escalate the problem and what level to escalate it to.

• Occasional Overtime and on standby

• MIE, clear criminal and credit
• Driver’s license and own reliable transport

• Market related salary

POLICY RESEARCHER & WRITER
Independent Contractor - Public Policy Think Tank - Bedfordview, Gauteng (Hybrid)
ABOUT THE ORGANISATION
Our client is a Non-Profit Organisation (NPO), a policy think tank, dedicated to inter alia, promoting free-market economics, individual liberty, freedom of choice, freedom of the press, speech and other human liberties. Funded by philanthropists and donors, the organisation works often behind the scenes to influence policymakers, media, and public opinion, advocating constructively for practical, market-based solutions on issues such as energy, labour law, land reform, healthcare (NHI), unemployment, just to name a few.
THE ROLE
We're looking for a Policy Researcher & Writer to research, develop, and publicly champion policy positions grounded in free-market principles. This is not a back-office research role, you will be the public face of the organisation's ideas: writing submissions to parliament, publishing articles, and appearing on radio and TV to argue the case for the policies you help develop.

Dis-Chem Pharmacies has an opportunity available for a Pharmacist Intern for their Matlosana store. The purpose of this Internship is to equip learners to understand the underlying principles of all of the major areas related to the pharmaceutical environment and promoting the notion of quality lifelong learning.The provision of pharmaceutical care by taking responsibility for the patients medicine related needs and being accountable for meeting these needs.To provide excellent customer service
Minimum Requirements:
Essential:
• Grade 12 / Matric
• BPharm - 4 year
• Computer literate – MS Office Advantageous:
• Work during degree – holiday work
• Unisolve and E-Scripting.Function and Duties:
• Pharmacist intern may provide or perform all the services or acts pertaining to the scope of practice of a pharmacist's assistant registered in the category pharmacist's assistant (post-basic) under the direct personal supervision of a pharmacist in a pharmacy.
• the sale of Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 medicines or scheduled substances;
• assist with the compounding, manipulation or preparation of a non-sterile or sterile medicine or scheduled substance according to a formula and Standard Operating Procedures approved by the responsible pharmacist;
• assist with the manufacturing of a non-sterile or sterile medicine or scheduled substance according to a formula and Standard Operating Procedures approved by the responsible pharmacist;
• the re-packaging of medicine;
• the distribution and control of stock of Schedule 1 to Schedule 6 medicines or scheduled substances;
• the ordering of medicine and scheduled substances up to and including Schedule 6 according to an instruction of a person authorised in terms of the Medicines Act to purchase or obtain such medicine or scheduled substance;
• the reading and preparation of a prescription, the selection, manipulation or compounding of the medicine, the labelling and supply of the medicine in an appropriate container following the interpretation and evaluation of the prescription by a pharmacist;
• the provision of instructions regarding the correct use of medicine supplied; and
• the provision of information to individuals in order to promote health.
• Pharmacist intern may, for the purposes of education and training, provide or perform all of the services or acts pertaining, to the scope of practice of a pharmacist under the direct personal supervision of a pharmacist in a pharmacy
• Accurately interpret scripts and act in a professional and responsible manner and within the legal requirements in accordance with the South African Pharmaceutical Counsel.
• Capture script details accurately and verify patient’s details on the system.
• Ensure accurate picking / packing / labeling off medication and be aware of common dosages as well as important drug interactions.
• Give accurate instructions to the patients regarding the correct use of medicine supplied.
• Keep abreast of changes in medical aid procedures and requirements for claims and dispensing.
• Ensure that all prescriptions entered, are checked for accuracy by a pharmacist and signed by a pharmacist.
• Advise and assist patients at the dispensary, self-medication counter and front-shop.
• Follow up with patients regarding script tracking report as requested by the dispensary manager.
• Explain all medical aid cost to patients, including difference between medical aid and cash / shelf price, if applicable.
• Process all paperwork necessary for the accurate submission of claims to medical aids.
• Correct errors on scripts rejected by medical aid.
• Ensure authorization of chronic, HIV and AIDS and oncology medication.
• Maintain customer profiles on the system.
• Take note of any messages on the customer profile and take suitable action.
• Report on low - / out of stock levels and stock errors to the dispensary manager.
• Assist with scheduled stock takes.
• Exercise stock and asset control.
• Housekeeping must be in accordance to Dis-Chem standards.
• Adhere to Dis-Chem Policies and Procedures and Standard Operating Procedures.
• Adhere to Health and Safety rules and regulations.
• Adhere to Dis-Chem Uniform and personal appearance policy. Competencies:
Essential:
• English and second language – Read, write and speak
• Application of knowledge gained as per university B.Pharm curriculum
• Good communication skills, listening skills
• Customer service/focus
• Conflict management
• Strong attention to detail
• Sound numerical skills
• Problem-solving
• Team player
• Trustworthy and honest
• Time management and adherence to deadline
• Able to deal with pressure
• Computer literate – MS Office Advantageous:
• Knowledge of Retail/ FMCG operations
• 3rd Additional Language
• Drug and family planning, and complementary medicine Special conditions of employment:
• Willing and able to work retail hours
• Controlled room temperature, security, limited space, health and safety, risk stock
• Physically fit and able to stand for long periods
• Valid driver’s license and own reliable transport
• Registered with Pharmacy Council – South African or valid work permit
• Clear credit and criminal records Remuneration and benefits:
• Market-related salaryONLY SUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS WILL BE CONTACTED. IF YOU HAVEN`T BEEN CONTACTED WITHIN TWO WEEKS AFTER THE CLOSING DATE CONSIDER YOUR APPLICATION AS UNSUCCESSFUL.

Dis-Chem Pharmacies has an opportunity available for a Pharmacist Intern for their Norwood store. The purpose of this Internship is to equip learners to understand the underlying principles of all of the major areas related to the pharmaceutical environment and promoting the notion of quality lifelong learning.The provision of pharmaceutical care by taking responsibility for the patients medicine related needs and being accountable for meeting these needs.To provide excellent customer service
Minimum Requirements:
Essential:
• Grade 12 / Matric
• BPharm - 4 year
• Computer literate – MS Office Advantageous:
• Work during degree – holiday work
• Unisolve and E-Scripting.Function and Duties:
• Pharmacist intern may provide or perform all the services or acts pertaining to the scope of practice of a pharmacist's assistant registered in the category pharmacist's assistant (post-basic) under the direct personal supervision of a pharmacist in a pharmacy.
• the sale of Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 medicines or scheduled substances;
• assist with the compounding, manipulation or preparation of a non-sterile or sterile medicine or scheduled substance according to a formula and Standard Operating Procedures approved by the responsible pharmacist;
• assist with the manufacturing of a non-sterile or sterile medicine or scheduled substance according to a formula and Standard Operating Procedures approved by the responsible pharmacist;
• the re-packaging of medicine;
• the distribution and control of stock of Schedule 1 to Schedule 6 medicines or scheduled substances;
• the ordering of medicine and scheduled substances up to and including Schedule 6 according to an instruction of a person authorised in terms of the Medicines Act to purchase or obtain such medicine or scheduled substance;
• the reading and preparation of a prescription, the selection, manipulation or compounding of the medicine, the labelling and supply of the medicine in an appropriate container following the interpretation and evaluation of the prescription by a pharmacist;
• the provision of instructions regarding the correct use of medicine supplied; and
• the provision of information to individuals in order to promote health.

TWK Agri has the following vacancy available: Financial Manager within the Financial Services division at Pretoria, Gauteng.
Job Summary
The Financial Manager is responsible for overseeing all financial activities, ensuring the financial health of the organisation, and providing strategic guidance to senior management. This role involves managing financial planning, reporting, budgeting, compliance functions, working capital, process optimisation, internal controls, pricing strategies, and production cost monitoring to optimise financial performance.
Responsibilities and Duties
• Develop and implement financial strategies aligned with business goals
• Conduct financial analysis and modelling to assess risks and opportunities
• Prepare and present financial forecasts and reports to senior management
• Assist the Finance Executive and lead the annual budgeting process with input from department heads
• Monitor budget performance and provide variance analysis with recommendations
• Revise forecasts to reflect changing business conditions
• Ensure accurate and timely preparation of financial statements (monthly, quarterly, annual)
• Oversee financial report consolidation across business units
• Maintain compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements
• Manage cash flow and ensure adequate liquidity for operations
• Develop cash flow forecasts and optimise working capital
• Monitor receivables, payables, and inventory to improve cash cycles
• Identify financial risks and implement mitigation strategies
• Ensure adherence to internal controls, policies, and regulations
• Coordinate and support internal and external audits
• Manage capital expenditure projects in line with strategic goals
• Monitor ROI and performance of key investments
• Develop and manage competitive, profit-focused pricing strategies
• Ensure pricing accuracy and maintain pricing controls
• Develop and maintain cost control systems and procedures to monitor organisational expenditure
• Analyse operational and overhead costs to identify inefficiencies and recommend improvements
• Ensure cost allocations are accurate and aligned with business activities
• Review and enhance financial processes for efficiency and accuracy
• Implement best practices and innovative solutions across teams
• Design, implement, and update internal control systems
• Train staff on control procedures and ensure compliance
• Lead and mentor the finance team to drive continuous improvement
• Conduct performance reviews and support professional development
• Communicate financial insights to non-financial stakeholders
• Prepare board presentations and align finance with organisational goals
Qualifications and Skills
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting or a related field
• Professional certification (CA(SA))
• 5 – 7 years’ experience in a financial management role
• Extensive knowledge of financial management principles and practices
• Understanding of the industry and its financial dynamics
• Familiarity with financial regulations, compliance standards and risk management
• Proficiency in financial software and tools
• Strong leadership and team management skills
• Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills

Join the MasterPiece Puzzles Team!
MasterPiece Puzzles is a rapidly growing, proudly South African puzzle brand creating beautifully designed, premium wooden puzzles with a strong focus on artwork, quality and standout packaging.
We’re a small, ambitious team based in Cape Town, working across a group of creative South African businesses including Matthew Bell Art, Roam and The Wood Lab — and we’re looking for a creative, organised and commercially minded person to join us and help take MasterPiece to its next stage of growth.
This is a varied, hands-on role, with a particular focus on growing and managing our wholesale business and various brand collaborations. You’ll work closely with our stockists, help us find and approach new stores, coordinate orders and launches, and make sure MasterPiece is represented beautifully wherever our products are sold. Big advantage if you are proficient in Photoshop, Illustrator, Canva and Shopify.
At the same time, you’ll be involved in the creative side of the brand — from new products and packaging to content, photoshoots and marketing. We’re a small team, so this is a role for someone who enjoys getting involved, taking ownership and making things happen.
What you’ll be doing
• Managing and growing our relationships with existing wholesale stockists
• Identifying and approaching potential new stockists across South Africa
• Following up on wholesale leads, enquiries and opportunities
• Helping coordinate wholesale orders, launches, catalogues and product information
• Helping ensure MasterPiece displays and products look great in stores
• Assisting with day-to-day operations, stock, production and packaging design
• Helping create and launch new products and collections
• Assisting with photoshoots, content creation, social media and marketing
• Working with customers, suppliers and our wider creative team
• Bringing new ideas and looking for opportunities to grow the brand
• Bringing energy, creativity, and fresh thinking to the brand
What we’re looking for
• Someone highly organised, proactive and reliable
• A confident, friendly communicator who enjoys building relationships
• A person who can manage follow-ups and keep multiple projects moving
• A creative eye and genuine interest in beautiful products, art and design
• Someone commercially minded who gets excited about growing sales and the business
• Experience in wholesale, sales, retail, marketing or e-commerce would be a big advantage
• Someone who enjoys learning, taking responsibility and being part of a small, ambitious team Why you’ll love it here
You won’t be stepping into a narrow corporate role. You’ll be joining a small entrepreneurial team where you’ll get exposure to product development, wholesale, marketing, e-commerce, operations and brand building.
Your ideas will matter, you’ll be trusted with real responsibility, and you’ll have the opportunity to grow your role as MasterPiece grows.
MasterPiece is part of a group of creative South African businesses, so there is plenty of variety, collaboration and opportunity to learn along the way.

Expeditors make sure procurement aligns with the project schedule. If something is late, they escalate and push for faster turnaround.

When delays or shortages occur, the expeditor finds solutions—alternative suppliers, revised delivery plans, or prioritising critical items.

They maintain records of orders, delivery dates, and supplier performance, and provide regular updates to project managers or procurement teams.

- Record Keeping & Governance: Maintain strict filing systems, support audit compliance, and guarantee that all financial and personal data tasks are conducted with the utmost confidentiality and integrity.

- Experience: Minimum of 3 years' stable experience in commerce and industry handling combined payroll administration and financial accounting duties.
- Attributes: High level of numeric accuracy, meticulous attention to detail, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to work effectively under pressure to meet strict deadlines.
- References: Must supply contactable professional references from previous employers (Financial Managers or CFOs you directly reported to) for verification.

- Annual Bonus: Paid in December in accordance with MICFA Regulations (pro-rata based on months of employment; not included in the starting basic salary).
- Leave Days: 18 days leave per annum.
- Probation: A 3-month probation period applies to monitor performance prior to permanent appointment.
Working Hours & Environment
- Standard Hours: Monday to Friday, 08:00 – 17:00 (Daily lunch break of 60 minutes).
- Overtime: Requested as required by the nature of the business, paid as per the MIBCO Agreement regarding the BCEA salary threshold.

• Drive client adoption

BACKGROUND:
African Parks is a non-profit conservation organisation that takes on responsibility for the long-term management of protected areas in partnership with governments and local communities. African Parks manages 24 protected areas in 13 countries covering over 20 million hectares.
In South Sudan, African Parks supports the management of the Great Nile Migration Landscape (GNML), centred around Badingilo National Park, Boma National Park, and the Jonglei landscape. Covering more than 120,000 km², the landscape supports the world’s largest remaining terrestrial mammal migration and is of major ecological importance regionally and globally
JOB OVERVIEW:

• Minimise exposure to obsolete, excess, and slow-moving inventory

Company Overview
Lesaka is a leading South African financial technology company. We deliver financial services to consumers (B2C) and merchants (B2B) in Southern Africa through our proprietary banking and payment technologies. About the role
We are seeking a Treasury Manager who will report directly to the Group Treasurer and serve as a senior execution partner across Lesaka's funding, liquidity and financial risk agenda. The role will take day-to-day ownership of debt facilities and covenant monitoring, strengthen cash and liquidity management across the Group, and support the management of interest rate and foreign exchange exposures. The successful candidate must combine technical treasury depth with disciplined execution, sound commercial judgement and the ability to work across a complex group structure.
Key Responsibilities
1.  Debt funding and working capital management
• Manage the Group's debt portfolio, including revolving credit, working capital, overdraft, guarantee and other committed or uncommitted facilities.
• Maintain a complete view of facility limits, utilisation, pricing, maturity profiles, security, guarantees and key contractual obligations.
• Prepare funding requirements and utilisation requests, coordinate drawdowns and repayments, and confirm that funding is available when required.
• Own the covenant monitoring process, including calculation review, sensitivity testing, compliance certificates and the evidence supporting lender submissions.
• Track undertakings, reporting deadlines, and other obligations under funding agreements.
• Build and maintain effective relationships with lenders, facility agents, debt advisers, legal advisers.
• Partner with business units and finance teams to understand working capital drivers and identify practical opportunities to release cash and reduce funding costs.2.  Liquidity and cash management
• Maintain reliable daily and forward-looking visibility of cash, available facilities and liquidity headroom across the Group.
• Manage and improve cash pooling, sweeping, offset, netting and intercompany funding arrangements within legal, tax, regulatory and facility constraints.
• Optimise the allocation of surplus cash and short-term borrowings to reduce interest expense and improve returns within approved risk limits.
• Oversee bank account structures, signatories, mandates, bank fees and cash management services in partnership with finance, legal and operational teams.
• Provide timely liquidity reporting to the Group Treasurer and senior management, highlighting forecast pressure points, concentration risk and available mitigants.3.  Interest rate and foreign exchange risk management
• Identify, quantify and report the Group's interest rate and foreign exchange exposures, including exposures arising from debt, cash flows, acquisitions and cross-border operations.
• Support the design and execution of approved hedging strategies using appropriate instruments, including swaps, forwards and options where relevant.
• Monitor hedge positions, counterparty limits, valuations, settlements and documentation, including ISDA and related confirmations where applicable.
• Work with Finance and Accounting to support accurate accounting, valuation, disclosure and control over treasury instruments.4.  Cash flow forecasting and treasury technology
• Own and continuously improve short-term and medium-term cash flow forecasting, including variance analysis, forecast accuracy and clear accountability for business inputs.
• Translate business plans, working capital trends, debt service and transaction activity into an integrated liquidity and funding forecast.
• Support the selection, implementation and effective use of a treasury management system and related bank connectivity, reporting and workflow tools.
• Improve the quality, timeliness and automation of treasury data, dashboards and management reporting.5.  Governance, controls and stakeholder support
• Operate within approved treasury policies, delegated authorities, facility agreements and regulatory requirements, and recommend updates where controls or operating needs change.
• Support internal and external audit requests and ensure that findings are resolved within agreed timelines.
• Provide treasury input into acquisitions, disposals, new products and other strategic initiatives, with a focus on funding, liquidity and financial risk implications.
• Act as a trusted treasury partner to Group Finance, business unit finance teams, Legal, Tax, Risk, Operations and executive stakeholders.Experience
• At least 7 years of relevant treasury experience, with substantial exposure to a complex corporate group, financial institution or similarly regulated environment.
• Strong practical experience in corporate debt funding, facility management, covenant monitoring and lender engagement.
• Demonstrated experience in liquidity management, cash pooling, cash concentration or offset arrangements and working capital optimisation.
• Practical knowledge of interest rate and foreign exchange risk management, including hedging instruments and transaction execution.
• Experience building or operating cash flow forecasts and producing decision-useful treasury reporting.
• Hands-on experience with a treasury management system, online banking platforms and ERP or financial reporting systems.
• Advanced Excel and financial modelling capability. Experience with data visualisation or reporting automation will be advantageous.Technical knowledge
• Corporate funding instruments, debt documentation, guarantees, security structures and covenant frameworks.
• Liquidity risk management, cash pooling, intercompany funding and short-term investment principles.
• Interest rate and foreign exchange markets, derivatives, confirmations, settlements and counterparty risk.
• Treasury accounting concepts, financial controls and relevant regulatory considerations, including exchange control where applicable.
• Treasury systems, bank connectivity, cash forecasting methods and management information design.Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related discipline.
• A relevant postgraduate qualification or professional designation such as CA(SA), ACT, CFA or FRM will be advantageous.Key working relationships
Internal stakeholders include the Group Treasurer, CFO and executive management, Group Finance, business unit finance teams, Legal, Tax, Risk, Operations, Internal Audit and M&A or strategic projects. External stakeholders include relationship banks, lenders, facility agents, debt advisers, legal advisers, auditors, treasury technology providers and other financial service providers.
Role context
This is a hands-on senior treasury role. It requires a person who can independently manage detailed funding and liquidity processes while also providing concise analysis and recommendations to the Group Treasurer. The role will suit someone who is comfortable working across multiple legal entities, responding to time-sensitive requirements and helping to strengthen a centralised Group Treasury capability.
